All eleven findings fixed and recorded in rewrite/findings/outcomes/step4-rules-fix-3.json; confirmation ran 101 commands against real git under sh and dash with no finding.

fix.summary: Fixed all 14 findings (S4R-rules-C1-1, S4R-rules-C1-2, S4R-rules-C2-2, S4B-rules-2, step4-rules-fix-3-C1-1..C1-10) by rebuilding how the merge-guard rule decides, adding a 46-case confirmation battery against real git under sh and dash (0 findings), rewriting the spec's What-it-checks, and recording the outcomes in rewrite/findings/outcomes/step4-rules-fix-3-2.json. The merge-guard judgement is now wholly positive: git-bearing by whole parsed words, plain by GIT_COMMANDS membership with per-verb full-spelling option tables and configuration-redirect detection, judged at the place git acts (threaded -C, last --git-dir via realpath, wrapper --chdir), with a bounded position test (cd words, case-folded guarded names on macOS, unplaced segments with reach in text) covering what the parse cannot read; heredoc bodies ride shell-reader segments, free-text values are message text everywhere, and tests-first extends the could-be-the-edit stance to delegated writers, expansion operands and cd-bearing opaque segments. The twelve step-3 test failures named in the task were already green when I ran the suite (another round's work) and stayed green; test_latency.py passed within the whole-suite run, so no solo timing run was needed; no foreign failures observed.

still_open.problem:
The -m/-F forms are fixed. Two gaps remain. (1) A free-text value is recognised only after a bare -m/-F or attached -mX, --message= or --file=. A short-option bundle ending in m is not read. So these are blocked opaque_git in the story worktree, while real git commits on the story branch: git commit -am "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: retry the fetch
EOF
)", git commit -sm "...the checkout step...", git commit -qam "...keep main green...", git add -A && git commit -am "...chore: branch cleanup...". (2) Mutating _segment_chunks to keep free-text values in the position scan fails no test (34 passed).
still_open.proposed_fix: Read a short bundle whose first m or F letter takes the rest of the word, or else the next word, as its free-text value (-am, -qam, -sm, -vF). Add -am/-sm/-qam heredoc messages naming fetch/checkout/branch/main as passing story-worktree cases. Add a not-plain git call whose only far word is in its message (FOO=$HOME git commit -m 'fix: retry the fetch') as a passing case, so the scan exclusion is tested.

still_open.problem: The ledger's measured git -c 'alias.p=push origin HEAD:develop' p passes from the story worktree, and real git (sh, dash) pushes develop. git -c alias.p=push p origin HEAD:develop does the same. The test runs it only on the main checkout, where position blocks. The position scan misses the far verb inside alias.p=push and the :develop of a refspec: _chunk_names matches name, */name and name: only. Separately, none of these checks has a test that fails without it (a scratch copy stays green): the GIT_COMMANDS check, _config_directed and the git-config-write check.
still_open.proposed_fix: A -c, --config-env or GIT_CONFIG_* key that redirects a verb (alias.*, push.*, remote.*.push) never passes on position: block opaque_git. Make _chunk_names also match <src>:<name> and <src>:refs/heads/<name>. Add as blocked cases: both alias pushes from the story worktree; a lone aliased verb on the main checkout (git ci -m x with the alias already configured); and from the story worktree, git -c remote.origin.push=HEAD:refs/heads/develop push origin and git config remote.origin.push ... && git push origin.

still_open.problem: (1) The CDPATH test in _cd_target is dead: `not resolved.startswith('/')` is never true. The measured export CDPATH=<parent>; cd <rootname> && git commit passes from the worktree and commits on develop (sh, dash). So does the prefix form CDPATH=<parent> cd <rootname>. tests-first: export CDPATH=<root>/.worktrees; cd S-9.01 && perl -pi ... changes the frozen test. The suite's CDPATH row blocks for another reason. (2) Only the segment opening a function body with { is marked. f() { :; git commit ...; }; cd <root> && f passes and commits on develop, as do a multi-line body, function f {...} and f() ( ... ). (3) A -C to a directory that does not exist yet is taken as a known place in no project: git worktree add -f <out>/x develop && git -C <out>/x commit (and the main-branch form from a directory in no project) moves the branch. (4) -C is resolved lexically but git chdirs physically: git -C <link-to-wt>/../.. commit from a neutral directory commits on develop. (5) Dropping realpath from _resolve_dir fails no test.
still_open.proposed_fix: Test the cd operand as typed for CDPATH, and honour a CDPATH assignment on the cd's own segment. Mark every segment between a function's { or ( and its close as body (where "", not plain). Give a -C or --git-dir target that does not exist at parse time where "". Resolve an existing -C with realpath. Add each measured command as a blocked case, using a CDPATH row that sh itself follows and a symlink to <root>/.git made before the call.

still_open.problem: The rest of a here-document opener's line is dropped from the parse. Measured (sh, dash). After red: cat <<'EOF' > tests/test_sample.py and cat <<'EOF' | tee tests/test_sample.py overwrite the frozen test and pass. Before red: cat <<'EOF' > src/new_module.py passes, while cat > src/new_module.py <<'EOF' blocks. From the worktree: git commit -F - <<'EOF' && git push origin HEAD:develop and cat <<'EOF' && git push origin HEAD:develop push develop. On the main checkout: cat <<'EOF' >/dev/null; git commit ... commits on develop. No test puts text after an opener.
still_open.proposed_fix: Keep the text from the end of the delimiter word to the newline in the cleaned text, and start bodies after that newline, in order for several openers. Add test_shell rows asserting that the redirect and the segment after && survive. Add the tests-first and merge-guard cases above.

still_open.problem: Only an exact sh with a -c word is opaque. Since the C1-8 fix, a command-string argument is read only when it holds a joiner; before, the whole-text split caught these, so for merge-guard this is a regression. Each of these passes while real git moves a guarded branch. From the worktree: bash -c 'git push origin HEAD:develop', sh -ec, dash -c, zsh -c, timeout 10 bash -c, echo '...' | sh, cat <<'EOF' | sh. On root: bash -lc 'git commit ...', printf '...' | bash. From a directory in no project: bash -c 'git -C <root> commit ...'. tests-first (after red): bash -c "perl -pi ... tests/test_sample.py", sh -ec, echo ... | sh, and bash -c 'cd <wt> && perl -pi ...' from root all change the frozen test.
still_open.proposed_fix: Make a segment opaque when its program's basename is sh/bash/dash/zsh/ksh and an option before the first operand carries c (-c, -ec, -lc, -xc, -c --). Make a shell reading a pipe or a here-document, with no -c and no script, carry the feeding text. Add the cases to test_merge_guard and test_tests_first.

still_open.problem: The C1-9 fix counts any argument naming a writer as a delegated write. After red, as the implementer, these read-only or legitimate commands are blocked red_test_frozen, and before red no_red_evidence: grep -rn rm src, grep -rw sed tests, which sed, python3 -c 'print(1)' touch, git mv src/module.py src/module2.py, git rm -q src/module.py.
still_open.proposed_fix: Count a delegation only where a word runs as a program: after a runner's options (flock, caffeinate, script, xargs, the wrapper table), after find -exec/-execdir/-ok, or first in a loop body. Judge git rm/mv by their operands. Add these as passing cases after red.

still_open.problem: An earlier segment that checks out another branch at the same place is not seen. From the worktree each passes, and real git moves the branch: git checkout main && git commit --allow-empty -m x; git switch -q main && git commit; git checkout -q main && git merge -q --no-edit story/S-9.01; git checkout main && git reset --hard story/S-9.01; git checkout --ignore-other-worktrees develop && git commit.
still_open.proposed_fix: Thread a per-place branch through the segments. A checkout or switch (not a pathspec checkout) sets it to the branch named. An unliteral name or another HEAD-changing verb makes it unknown, and an unknown branch is judged as guarded. Add these cases, plus git checkout -- src/x.py && git commit as a passing case.

still_open.problem: Each passes while real git moves a guarded branch. From the worktree: git push origin HEAD:heads/develop and HEAD:heads/main; git push origin 'refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*', 'refs/heads/*' and the matching refspec :, which push develop and main; git fetch origin '+refs/heads/m*:refs/heads/m*', which resets main. On root: git update-ref HEAD story/S-9.01 and git update-ref -d HEAD, which move or delete develop through the HEAD symref; the same via git -C <root> from the worktree.
still_open.proposed_fix: Read a destination as guarded when it is <name>, heads/<name> or refs/heads/<name> (case-folded on macOS). Make wildcard refspecs and bare :/+: block as --all does. Read HEAD and @ in update-ref/symbolic-ref (without --no-deref) as the branch HEAD names. Add these cases.

still_open.problem: Option values are read as operands. On develop each passes and moves develop: git push -o ci.skip origin and --push-option ci.skip origin, against a remote that accepts push options (the value is taken for the remote, so the bare push is missed); git checkout --conflict merge -B develop story/S-9.01; git checkout story/S-9.01 -B develop. From the worktree: git rebase story/S-9.01 main -X theirs and --exec true rewrite main.
still_open.proposed_fix: Mark the separate-value options of each governed verb (push -o/--push-option/--repo/--receive-pack/--exec; checkout/switch -b/-B/-c/-C/--orphan/--conflict; rebase -x/--exec/-X/-s/--onto) and consume their values. Read the branch from -B/-C/--force-create's own value. Add the six cases.

still_open.problem: A builtin that moves the current shell in an earlier segment is not read as a cd. From the worktree each passes, and git commits on develop: eval cd <root>; git commit (sh, dash); builtin cd <root> && git commit (sh); source /dev/stdin <<<"cd <root>"; git commit (sh). tests-first from root after red: eval cd <wt>; perl -pi ... and builtin cd <wt> && perl -pi ... change the frozen test.
still_open.proposed_fix: After an eval, builtin, source or . segment whose text holds cd, pushd or popd, set where "" for later segments. Read builtin cd as cd. Add the cases to both rules' tests.

still_open.problem: Brace expansion is read as literal text; macOS sh (bash), bash and zsh expand it. These pass and move a guarded branch: git push origin HEAD:dev{elop,} and git branch -f {main,HEAD} (sh, bash, zsh); cd {<root>,} && git commit (sh); git -C {<root>,} commit (sh, bash). tests-first: perl -pi ... tests/test_{sample,x}.py changes the frozen test (sh).
still_open.proposed_fix: Mark an unquoted {...} holding a top-level comma or .. as expanded, like a glob, so the word is not literal and the path is not nameable. Add the cases.

still_open.problem: A non-literal program word is never git-bearing. From the worktree each passes, and git (sh, dash) pushes develop: G=git; $G push origin HEAD:develop; git$(echo) push ...; $(printf gi)t push ...; /usr/bin/gi? push ...; alias g=git followed on the next line by g push .... On root: G=git; $G commit commits on develop. tests-first: G=perl; $G -pi -e ... tests/test_sample.py changes the frozen test.
still_open.proposed_fix: Treat a program word holding an expansion, a substitution or a glob as git-bearing and not plain (position decides), and as an unreadable write. Let an alias whose value names git or a writer poison later segments. Add the cases.
